messages.content: Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.
Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating-point numbers have a finite precision, so when two operands are added the result is rounded to the nearest representable value. Because rounding can discard low‑order bits, the intermediate sum in \((a+b)+c\) may lose information that would affect the final result, while the sum \(a+(b+c)\) rounds a different intermediate value. Consequently the two possible groupings can produce different rounded results, breaking the associativity property that holds for exact real arithmetic.

Floating-point numbers have a finite precision, so each operation rounds the exact real sum to the nearest representable value. Because rounding can discard low‑order bits, the intermediate result of \((a+b)+c\) may lose information that would affect the final sum, while \(a+(b+c)\) rounds a different intermediate value and can retain different bits. Consequently the two rounded results can differ, showing that floating‑point addition is not associative.
